column1: What counts as cannibalization here: a query where 2 or more of your URLs each got 3+ impressions at an average position of 50 or better in the export period. 540 queries showed 2+ URLs in total; 166 meet this bar and are listed in Query Map.
#section links (e.g. /best-property-management-software-in-canada/#what-is-pms) were folded into their page. They are the same page, not cannibalization.

Owner page: chosen by search intent (cost → cost post; small business → small-business page; best/top/companies → listicle; packages/plans/monthly → packages page; WordPress, eCommerce, Shopify, white-label, country, repair, support → their own pages; generic "website maintenance services/company" → homepage).

Rows from URLs without a trailing slash were left out: they are duplicate copies of slash URLs that show up as homepage sitelinks, not separate competing pages. They are listed as a technical fix in the Action Plan.

"Not ranking yet" means the correct owner is not ranking for that query today. Those owners must be strengthened before you de-optimize the page that currently ranks; do the Priority 1 "Strengthen owner" rows first.

Order of work: 1) Merges and 301s. 2) Strengthen owner pages. 3) De-optimize the competing pages. 4) Change internal links so the exact-match anchor always points to the owner. 5) Request indexing in Search Console and re-run this export after 4–6 weeks.
When you merge: move any unique, useful content first, keep the stronger URL, 301 the weaker one, update every internal link to the new URL, and remove the old URL from the sitemap.
